newsitem.title: USA: Cooler temperatures aid California firefighters.
newsitem.headline: Cooler temperatures aid California firefighters.

text.p: Firefighters on Sunday said they gained the upper hand on a wildfire along a scenic stretch of California coast, allowing evacuated residents to return to their homes and businesses to reopen.

Cooler temperatures and a drop in the winds have aided fire crews battling the blaze, which broke out on Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.
The fire, burning in the Ventana wilderness area of the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty, has now consumed some 668 acres (270 hectares), fire officials estimated.
Firefighters said, however, that the blaze was 80 percent contained, an improvement over Saturday evening's 45 percent. Firefighters said they expect full containment Monday evening.
"We made excellent progress today," fire information officer David Schreiner said.

Firefighters have lifted an evacuation order for houses and businesses along a five-mile (eight-km) stretch on the east side of Highway One, a popular route that winds along the California coast, said fire information officer Larry Hornberger.
"Things are returning to normal," he said.
The fire no longer immediately threatened about 25 homes and a half-dozen businesses, including the well-known Ventana Inn, which lies about two miles (three kms) south of Big Sur.
A section of Highway One that was closed on Saturday was reopened on Sunday at noon, Hornberger said.
One travel trailer was destroyed in the blaze but so far no homes have been lost. Schreiner said one injury was reported.
Nearly 900 firefighters were battling the blaze, backed by four air tankers and eight helicopters. Some firefighters were being pulled from the fire lines due to progress by crews.
Officials estimated the cost to date of the multi-agency fire fighting effort at nearly $900,000, but said the total could reach $1.5 million.
The cause of the fire was still unknown and was under investigation.
